Brightness of light, in lux.Starlight, moonless night: On a clear moonless night your eyes need about half an hour to dark-adapt to the faint glow of starlight.
Brightness of light, in lux.Quarter moon: A quarter moon is far less than half as bright as a full moon, because shadows on its surface grow longer.
Brightness of light, in lux.Full moon: The full moon is no brighter than it is because the lunar surface is dark, reflecting only about 12 percent of the sunlight.
Brightness of light, in lux.Candle at 1 metre: The candela, the official unit of luminous intensity, gets its name from the candle that once served as the standard for measuring light.
Brightness of light, in lux.Street lighting: Many cities are swapping orange sodium streetlamps for white LEDs, which save energy but add blue light that scatters more in the night sky.
Brightness of light, in lux.Living room: A typical living room is dim yet feels bright, because the eye adjusts so well that it copes with a range of around a billion to one.
Brightness of light, in lux.Office: Around 500 lux is the usual recommendation for desk work. Light that is much weaker makes eyes work harder and tire sooner.
Brightness of light, in lux.Overcast day: Even a gray overcast day is several times brighter than a well-lit office, which is why a cloudy afternoon still feels bright after you step outside.
Brightness of light, in lux.Daylight, not direct sun: Photographers prize this soft light, found in open shade on a clear day, because it flatters faces without harsh shadows.
Brightness of light, in lux.Direct sunlight: Direct sun is about a billion times brighter than starlight, an enormous range that the human eye handles by adapting.

Cards in these card-game decks.Euchre deck: It has 24 cards, and the Joker was invented for this game as a trump card.
Cards in these card-game decks.Pinochle deck: Two copies of each card from nine to ace make up this meld-based game's deck.
Cards in these card-game decks.Standard deck, no jokers: Many say its 52 cards mirror the weeks of the year, though that is a folk idea.
Cards in these card-game decks.Standard deck with jokers: Jokers only entered American decks in the 1860s, and rules about them vary.
Cards in these card-game decks.Rook deck: Parker Brothers invented it in 1906 as an alternative for families who disapproved of regular playing cards.
Cards in these card-game decks.Pokémon TCG deck: Tournament rules cap decks at 60 cards and allow only four copies of any card except basic Energy.
Cards in these card-game decks.Tarot deck: Used in tarocchi in 15th-century Italy, it has 22 trump cards plus four suits.
Cards in these card-game decks.Set (the game): It has every combination of four features, and the most cards you can lay out without a set is 20.
Cards in these card-game decks.Classic Uno deck: A barber in Ohio invented it in 1971, and it has since sold hundreds of millions of decks.
Cards in these card-game decks.Skip-Bo deck: This descendant of the game Spite and Malice is played using 144 numbered cards plus 18 wild ones.

Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Broadside: A broadside is a single sheet printed on one side, and for centuries it was how ballads and proclamations were spread cheaply.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Folio: Shakespeare's First Folio of 1623 gathered his plays and saved about eighteen that might otherwise have been lost.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Quarto: Many of Shakespeare's plays first appeared as cheap quarto editions during his lifetime.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Octavo: Aldus Manutius popularised small octavo books in Venice around 1501, the ancestor of the pocket paperback.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Duodecimo: Often written 12mo, it produces handy small books; the twelve leaves make 24 pages.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Sextodecimo: Written 16mo, each leaf is one-sixteenth of the sheet, giving a book small enough for a pocket.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Vicesimo-quarto: Its name is Latin for twenty-fourth; books of this size are tiny and were popular as pocket editions.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Trigesimo-secundo: From the Latin for thirty-second, 32mo books are tiny enough to sit in the palm of a hand.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Quadragesimo-octavo: That is Latin for forty-eighth, and these books are miniature volumes, mostly seen in collections of miniature books.
Book formats, by leaves per printed shee.Sexagesimo-quarto: At 64mo a whole sheet becomes a tiny volume; miniature books of this size are collectors' items.

Countries by population.Fiji: It spreads across more than 300 islands, though most people live on the biggest, Viti Levu.
Countries by population.Portugal: Its land borders have barely changed since a treaty with Castile in 1297, among the oldest national borders in Europe.
Countries by population.Netherlands: About a quarter of the country lies below sea level, so dikes and pumps keep much of it dry.
Countries by population.Australia: Most of its people live along the coast, leaving the vast interior outback sparsely populated.
Countries by population.Spain: It is one of the world's most-visited countries, with Spanish, Catalan, Basque and Galician all official in various regions.
Countries by population.Germany: Europe's most populous country outside Russia, its capital Berlin was reunited with its eastern half only in 1990.
Countries by population.Russia: The largest country on Earth by area, it spans 11 time zones from Kaliningrad to Kamchatka.
Countries by population.Brazil: South America's largest country and the only one where Portuguese is the main language; it shelters most of the Amazon rainforest.
Countries by population.United States: It has the world's third-largest population, with its people spread across 50 states and several territories.
Countries by population.India: It overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023.

How many wheels?.Unicycle: Skilled riders play unicycle hockey and basketball, and some tackle rough mountain trails.
How many wheels?.Bicycle: Scientists still debate precisely why a moving bike stays upright; steering geometry matters more than gyroscopic effects.
How many wheels?.Tricycle: Queen Victoria reportedly bought tricycles, helping make them fashionable for adults.
How many wheels?.Car: Many new cars now skip a full spare tire and carry a repair kit instead.
How many wheels?.Office chair: The five-pointed base is standard because it keeps the chair far more stable than four legs would.
How many wheels?.Dually pickup truck: It is nicknamed a dually because of the double wheels on its rear axle, which carry heavy loads.
How many wheels?.Pair of roller skates: In 1760 Joseph Merlin glided into a London party on early skates, with a violin in hand, and crashed into a mirror.
How many wheels?.Semi truck: Its nickname, the eighteen-wheeler, comes from the tractor and trailer's 18 tires on the common five-axle layout.
How many wheels?.Airbus A380: It has 22 wheels, 20 under the body and 2 on the nose, to support the world's largest passenger jet.
How many wheels?.Antonov An-225: The Ukrainian giant, whose name Mriya means dream, was the heaviest aircraft ever built, with six engines and 32 wheels; it was destroyed in 2022.

US islands by area.Alcatraz: This San Francisco Bay island held a famous federal prison from 1934 to 1963, and its rocky isolation and cold currents made escape nearly impossible.
US islands by area.Manhattan: Manhattan's famous 1626 purchase for 24 dollars' worth of trade goods is probably a tidy myth, and the Lenape who lived here did not think of land as ownable.
US islands by area.Nantucket: This Massachusetts island's name comes from a Wampanoag word, and it was once the world's whaling capital, with Moby-Dick ties.
US islands by area.Martha's Vineyard: Jaws was filmed here in 1974, and its name may honor Martha, either the daughter or mother-in-law of explorer Bartholomew Gosnold.
US islands by area.Molokaʻi: This Hawaiian island, nicknamed 'the Friendly Isle', is home to the world's tallest sea cliffs, which rise over 1,000 m on its north coast.
US islands by area.Oʻahu: This Hawaiian island is home to Honolulu, Pearl Harbor and Waikiki, and it holds about two thirds of the state's people.
US islands by area.Maui: This Hawaiian island, nicknamed the Valley Isle, is where visitors watch humpback whales, and the Haleakala volcano's crater lies here.
US islands by area.Long Island: Long Island stretches about 190 km from Brooklyn out to Montauk, and it holds Brooklyn, Queens and two suburban counties, home to some 8 million people.
US islands by area.Kodiak Island: This Alaskan island is the home of the world's largest bears, the Kodiak brown bear, which can weigh up to about 600 kg.
US islands by area.Hawaiʻi (Big Island): Hawaii's biggest island is still growing, as Kilauea's lava flows add new land, and Mauna Kea rises more than 10,000 m from the sea floor.

When these ice cream brands were founded.Breyers: Founded in Philadelphia by William Breyer, who started by delivering ice cream by hand.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Good Humor: Harry Burt created the ice cream on a stick, and sold from trucks with bells.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Dairy Queen: The Blizzard debuted in 1985, and it's served upside-down to prove it's thick.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Baskin-Robbins: Known for 31 flavours, one for each day of the month, it was founded by brothers-in-law Burt Baskin and Irv Robbins.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Mister Softee: The Conway brothers founded it in Philadelphia, and its jingle is a familiar sound of ice cream trucks.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Häagen-Dazs: Its name was invented to sound Danish, and means nothing; the founder, Reuben Mattus, was from the Bronx.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Ben & Jerry's: Two friends started it in a renovated gas station in Burlington, Vermont, after a five-dollar ice cream course.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Dippin' Dots: Beads of ice cream are flash-frozen with liquid nitrogen, an idea by microbiologist Curt Jones.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Pinkberry: The Los Angeles chain started the frozen yogurt wave with a tart, minimalist style.
When these ice cream brands were founded.Halo Top: Low-calorie pints, with a sweet taste from sugar substitutes, made it the best-selling pint in America in 2017.

When these game companies were founded.Nintendo: Long before games, it made hanafuda playing cards in Kyoto, and the company still operates in the same city.
When these game companies were founded.Namco: Founded as Nakamura Manufacturing, it ran mechanical rides on department-store rooftops years before releasing Pac-Man in 1980.
When these game companies were founded.Konami: It began in Osaka renting and repairing jukeboxes, and much later gave the world Castlevania, Metal Gear and the famous Konami Code.
When these game companies were founded.Atari: Its name comes from a term in the board game Go, similar to saying 'check'; Pong was its first hit.
When these game companies were founded.Capcom: Its name is short for Capsule Computers, and it is the maker of Street Fighter, Resident Evil and Mega Man.
When these game companies were founded.Electronic Arts: Founded by Trip Hawkins, it early on marketed programmers like rock stars, with album-style packaging for its software.
When these game companies were founded.Square: It chose the name Final Fantasy because the company was close to bankruptcy and expected it to be its last game; it was a hit.
When these game companies were founded.Valve: Founded by two ex-Microsoft employees, Gabe Newell and Mike Harrington, it made Half-Life in 1998 and launched the Steam store in 2003.
When these game companies were founded.Rockstar Games: Made by Take-Two in New York, with brothers Sam and Dan Houser; it is the publisher of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption.
When these game companies were founded.Mojang: Markus 'Notch' Persson set it up to publish Minecraft, and Microsoft bought it in 2014 for about 2.5 billion dollars.

NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Shepard's Freedom 7: Alan Shepard's 15-minute suborbital flight made him the first American in space, 23 days after Yuri Gagarin.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Glenn's Friendship 7: John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth, circling three times, while controllers worried about a loose heat shield.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Gemini 4 spacewalk: Ed White floated outside on the first US spacewalk and was so reluctant to get back in that he had to be ordered inside.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 1 fire: A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal killed Grissom, White and Chaffee, and it led to a complete redesign of the capsule.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 8 circles the Moon: The crew became the first to circle the Moon, took the 'Earthrise' photo, and read from Genesis on Christmas Eve.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 11 lands: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the surface, leaving a plaque reading 'We came in peace for all mankind'.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 13 crisis: An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon, and the crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat to return safely.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 15 first rover drive: The crew became the first to drive on the Moon, and Commander Scott dropped a hammer and a feather to show they fall together.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Apollo 17, last Moonwalk: Gene Cernan was the last person to step off the Moon, and the crew took the 'Blue Marble' photo of the whole Earth.
NASA's road to the Moon and beyond.Skylab launches: America's first space station lost its micrometeoroid shield at launch, but crews repaired it, and it fell to Earth in 1979.

Pioneering feats by women.Ederle swims the Channel: She swam the Channel in 14 hours 39 minutes, faster than any man before her.
Pioneering feats by women.Earhart flies Atlantic solo: She vanished over the Pacific in 1937 while trying to fly around the world.
Pioneering feats by women.Tereshkova in space: Valentina Tereshkova is still the only woman to have flown a solo space mission.
Pioneering feats by women.Switzer runs Boston: She ran Boston as 'K. V. Switzer', and a race official tried to tear off her bib.
Pioneering feats by women.Tabei summits Everest: She later became the first woman to complete the Seven Summits, the highest peak on each continent.
Pioneering feats by women.Comaneci scores a perfect 10: At 14 she scored a perfect 10 at Montreal, and the scoreboard could only show 1.00.
Pioneering feats by women.Earle walks the seafloor: She walked untethered at 381 meters on the seafloor in a pressure suit, and is nicknamed Her Deepness.
Pioneering feats by women.Sally Ride in space: She later investigated both the Challenger and Columbia accidents and wrote children's science books.
Pioneering feats by women.Benoit wins Olympic marathon: She won the first women's Olympic marathon in Los Angeles, 17 days after knee surgery.
Pioneering feats by women.Nyad swims Cuba to Florida: She completed the 177 km swim at 64, without a shark cage, on her fifth attempt.

Triple Crown winning racehorses.Sir Barton: The first Triple Crown winner, in 1919, though the term only caught on in the 1930s. He won the Preakness just days after the Kentucky Derby.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Gallant Fox: Nicknamed "the Fox of Belair", the 1930 champion later sired Omaha, who won in 1935, the only father and son pair to both take the Triple Crown.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.War Admiral: A son of the great Man o' War, he won in 1937. In 1938 he lost a famous match race to Seabiscuit, in front of a huge radio audience.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Whirlaway: Called "Mr. Longtail" for his flowing tail, he was known for running wide on turns yet still won all three races in 1941.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Citation: The 1948 champion became the first horse to win a million dollars in career earnings, in 1951, a milestone for American racing.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Secretariat: His 31-length win in the 1973 Belmont set a record that still stands, and ended a 25-year drought. An autopsy found an unusually large heart.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Seattle Slew: In 1977 he became the only horse to win the Triple Crown while still undefeated, and he later raced into the next year.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Affirmed: His 1978 duel with rival Alydar, who finished second in all three races, is regarded as one of the greatest rivalries in racing.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.American Pharoah: He ended a 37-year drought in 2015. His odd spelling, "Pharoah", came from a mistake in the naming contest, and it was kept.
Triple Crown winning racehorses.Justify: The 2018 champion had not raced as a 2-year-old, which no Kentucky Derby winner had done since 1882, and he retired undefeated.

Fast food chains, by founding year.Nathan's Famous: The Coney Island stand began in 1916 and still holds a hot-dog eating contest every July 4, where winners eat dozens in ten minutes.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Domino's: Started in 1960 as DomiNick's in Michigan, it was bought by brothers Tom and James Monaghan and renamed. It built its name on 30-minute delivery.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Taco Bell: Glen Bell opened the first stand in 1962 in Downey, California. Its tacos began as a way to bring Mexican-style food to American drive-through customers.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Arby's: The roast beef chain founded by the Raffel brothers in Ohio in 1964 has a cowboy hat logo, and its slogan "We Have the Meats" became a pop-culture meme.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Popeyes: Founded in New Orleans in 1972 with a Louisiana-style spicy chicken, its name comes from a character in The French Connection, not from the cartoon sailor.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Jollibee: It began as an ice cream parlor in Manila in the 1970s and grew into the Philippines' biggest fast-food chain, outselling McDonald's there.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Panda Express: Founded by Andrew and Peggy Cherng in a Glendale, California, mall in 1983. Its signature orange chicken was created by a chef in 1987.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Five Guys: Named for the Murrell family's five sons, it began in Arlington, Virginia. It is known for hand-cut fries and free peanuts, and a bag of fries is overflowing.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Wingstop: Founded in Garland, Texas, it built its name on flavored chicken wings and a menu of about a dozen sauces and rubs, then grew worldwide.
Fast food chains, by founding year.Sweetgreen: Begun in 2007 in Washington, D.C. by three Georgetown University graduates, this chain made salads and grain bowls a fast-food category.

Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Moses: Tradition splits his 120 years into three phases of 40 years: in Egypt, in Midian and in the wilderness.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Abraham: He was buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Hebron, near his wife Sarah, by his sons Isaac and Ishmael.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Terah: Abraham's father, who set out from Ur for Canaan, but settled in Haran along the way.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Eber: The word 'Hebrew' is traditionally linked to his name, as he is an ancestor of the Hebrews.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Shem: Noah's son, and his name gave us the term 'Semitic' for a family of languages and peoples.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Lamech: Noah's father; his 777 years form a pattern of sevens, a number with deep meaning in the Bible.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Mahalalel: His Hebrew name means 'praise of God', and he is a link in the long genealogy from Adam to Noah.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Adam: The first man in Genesis, and his name is linked to 'adamah', the Hebrew word for earth or ground.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Noah: Per Genesis he lived 350 years after the Flood, and his story survives in Babylonian flood tales.
Biblical lifespans: the record holders.Methuselah: His name is a byword for extreme old age, shared by a bristlecone pine in California that is thousands of years old.

Scrabble score of these animal names.EEL: European eels are born in the Sargasso Sea, and travel thousands of kilometres to reach European rivers, and nobody has ever witnessed their spawning.
Scrabble score of these animal names.LION: Lions are the only truly social big cats, living in prides where the related females do most of the hunting.
Scrabble score of these animal names.CAT: Cats sleep for roughly two thirds of their lives, and purr at frequencies that may help bones and tissue heal.
Scrabble score of these animal names.PIG: Pigs are among the smartest farm animals, and have even been taught to play simple video games with a joystick.
Scrabble score of these animal names.HORSE: Horses can doze while standing because a locking system in their legs lets them rest without falling over.
Scrabble score of these animal names.WOLF: A wolf's howl can carry for several kilometres, and each pack member's voice is distinct enough for others to tell them apart.
Scrabble score of these animal names.DUCK: A gland near the tail makes oil that ducks spread through their feathers, which keeps the water from soaking through.
Scrabble score of these animal names.FOX: Red foxes seem to use Earth's magnetic field when pouncing, and tend to succeed most often when jumping toward the north-east.
Scrabble score of these animal names.JAGUAR: The jaguar's bite is among the strongest of any big cat for its size, powerful enough to crack open turtle shells.
Scrabble score of these animal names.ZEBRA: Every zebra's stripe pattern is unique, and the stripes are thought to confuse the biting flies that plague horses.

Medical and legal TV drama premieres.Perry Mason: Raymond Burr played the defense lawyer who nearly always won his case; the show ran for nine seasons and later spawned TV movies.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.M*A*S*H (TV): M*A*S*H's 1983 finale drew over 100 million US viewers, a television record that stood for decades; the show was set in the Korean War.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.L.A. Law: L.A. Law, created by Steven Bochco, ran for eight seasons and won the Emmy for best drama series four times.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.Law & Order: Law & Order ran for 20 seasons and its dramatic opening sound, the famous chung chung, became one of the most recognizable on TV.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.Ally McBeal: Ally McBeal mixed courtroom comedy with fantasy scenes, such as a dancing baby, and made Calista Flockhart a star.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.House: Hugh Laurie's Dr. House was inspired by Sherlock Holmes; his apartment is 221B, the same number as Holmes's Baker Street address.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.Grey's Anatomy: The show's title is a pun on Gray's Anatomy, the classic medical textbook, and it became one of the longest-running US primetime dramas.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.The Good Wife: Julianna Margulies stars as a politician's wife who returns to law practice; its spin-off The Good Fight kept the legal drama going.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.Suits: Set in a Manhattan firm, Suits starred Meghan Markle before she married Prince Harry, and it surged again when it hit Netflix in 2023.
Medical and legal TV drama premieres.The Pitt: The Pitt follows a single 15-hour emergency room shift, one hour per episode, with Noah Wyle, who earlier starred in ER.

Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Henry VII: Henry VII won the crown at Bosworth Field in 1485, beating Richard III and founding the Tudor dynasty.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Henry VIII: His six marriages and break with Rome created the Church of England.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Edward VI: Crowned at nine and dead at 15, his short reign pushed England firmly toward Protestant reform.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Mary I: She restored Catholicism and had about 280 Protestants burned, earning the nickname 'Bloody Mary'.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Elizabeth I: Her 44-year reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 and the flowering of Shakespeare.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.James I: Already James VI of Scotland, he united the crowns, and the King James Bible followed in 1611.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Charles I: Beheaded in 1649 after losing the civil war, he is the only English king ever executed.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Charles II: The 'Merry Monarch' returned in 1660 after the Commonwealth, reopening the theatres Puritans had closed.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.James II: A Catholic king, he was overthrown in the Glorious Revolution of 1688 and replaced by William and Mary.
Tudor and Stuart monarchs, by accession.Queen Anne: The last Stuart monarch, during her reign the 1707 Acts of Union created Great Britain; none of her 17 pregnancies produced a surviving heir.

Heights of New York City buildings.Flatiron Building: Opened in 1902, its triangular wedge shape gave it a nickname, and was among the tallest buildings in the city, at 22 stories.
Heights of New York City buildings.Seagram Building: Designed by Mies van der Rohe, this bronze-toned skyscraper became a model for modern glass-and-steel office towers.
Heights of New York City buildings.Woolworth Building: Frank Woolworth paid for this 'Cathedral of Commerce' in cash, and it was the world's tallest building from 1913 to 1930.
Heights of New York City buildings.30 Rockefeller Plaza: The centerpiece of Rockefeller Center is home to NBC's Tonight Show, and a famous Christmas tree stands nearby.
Heights of New York City buildings.Chrysler Building: Its Art Deco spire, clad in stainless steel, was briefly the world's tallest building, before the Empire State Building topped it in 1931.
Heights of New York City buildings.Bank of America Tower: A glass tower with a crystalline shape, it's known for being among the greenest skyscrapers in the US.
Heights of New York City buildings.Empire State Building: It rose in just over a year, and for decades was the world's tallest building, and King Kong famously climbed it.
Heights of New York City buildings.111 West 57th Street: Also known as Steinway Tower, it's the world's thinnest skyscraper, with a width-to-height ratio of about 1:24.
Heights of New York City buildings.Central Park Tower: This pencil-thin tower south of Central Park holds the record for the world's tallest residential building, and its apartments sell for tens of millions.
Heights of New York City buildings.One World Trade Center: Its height of 1,776 feet nods to the year of American independence, and it was built on the site of the Twin Towers.

James Bond films by release.Dr. No: Sean Connery introduced Bond to the screen in it, and the film was made on a budget of about a million dollars.
James Bond films by release.Goldfinger: The Aston Martin DB5 first appeared here, and the golden-painted victim became one of cinema's best-known images.
James Bond films by release.Thunderball: Much of the film is set underwater, and a legal fight over its story rights stretched for years.
James Bond films by release.You Only Live Twice: The screenplay was written by children's author Roald Dahl, and the villain's lair is hidden in a volcano in Japan.
James Bond films by release.Diamonds Are Forever: Sean Connery came back for a record salary, and he gave much of it to charity.
James Bond films by release.Live and Let Die: Roger Moore's first Bond film, with a title song by Paul McCartney that earned an Oscar nomination.
James Bond films by release.The Spy Who Loved Me: The Lotus Esprit that turns into a submarine is the star, and the film opens with a ski jump off a cliff.
James Bond films by release.Moonraker: It sent Bond into space even before the real Space Shuttle had flown, with laser battles between astronauts.
James Bond films by release.GoldenEye: After a six-year break, the new Bond Pierce Brosnan arrived, and a Nintendo 64 game based on it became a hit.
James Bond films by release.Casino Royale (Craig): Daniel Craig's first outing rebooted the series, and it adapted Ian Fleming's first novel, published in 1953.

Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Gutenberg printing press: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press let one workshop produce books that scribes needed months to copy; his Bible appeared around 1455.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.First surviving photograph: Nicephore Niepce's view from his window was exposed on a pewter plate coated with bitumen and needed many hours of sunlight.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Morse telegraph message: Sent from Washington to Baltimore, its text was 'What hath God wrought', chosen by a young woman, Annie Ellsworth, rather than by Morse himself.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Sholes typewriter: Christopher Sholes' machine, built and sold with Remington, popularised the QWERTY layout, usually said to have been arranged to stop typebars jamming.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Telephone: Alexander Graham Bell patented it in 1876, and rival Elisha Gray filed a similar claim at almost the same moment.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Edison's phonograph: Edison's first recordings were scratched onto tinfoil wrapped around a cylinder; he is said to have recited 'Mary had a little lamb' into it.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Gramophone record: Emile Berliner's flat disc beat the cylinder because copies could be pressed in bulk from a metal master.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Marconi's radio: Guglielmo Marconi first sent wireless signals over about two kilometres, past a hill, on his family's estate in Italy.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Baird's television demo: John Logie Baird's London demo used a spinning mechanical disc, a system soon beaten by electronic television.
Capturing words, sounds and pictures.Magnetic tape recorder: Germany's AEG Magnetophon used plastic tape coated with iron oxide, and after World War II its design spread through radio and music studios.

How tall can these plants grow?.Arctic willow: It hugs the ground, which shields the dwarf shrub from Arctic winds and keeps it tiny for a woody plant.
How tall can these plants grow?.Lavender: Its name comes from the Latin for 'to wash', and Romans scented their baths with it.
How tall can these plants grow?.Lilac: Lilacs belong to the olive family, and their fragrance is a spring highlight in many gardens.
How tall can these plants grow?.Apple tree: Each pip grows into a different variety, so orchards graft cuttings to make sure the fruit is as expected.
How tall can these plants grow?.Hawthorn: Its white May blossom gave rise to the name 'may tree', and its thorny branches make a dense hedge.
How tall can these plants grow?.Coconut palm: As a palm, it has no true wood and no growth rings, and its coconuts can float across oceans.
How tall can these plants grow?.English oak: An oak can support hundreds of insect species, more than any other native tree in Britain.
How tall can these plants grow?.Kapok tree: Its seed fluff, kapok, was once stuffed into life jackets because it floats so well.
How tall can these plants grow?.Giant sequoia: These trees are the largest living things by volume, and the General Sherman is the most massive of all.
How tall can these plants grow?.Coast redwood: The tallest known tree is a redwood called Hyperion, about 116 m, whose location is kept secret to protect it.

US states by total area.Rhode Island: Its official name was State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations until 2020.
US states by total area.West Virginia: It was formed in 1863 when counties broke away from Virginia during the Civil War.
US states by total area.Ohio: The birthplace of seven presidents, which earned it the nickname Mother of Presidents.
US states by total area.New York: Adirondack Park alone is larger than several national parks combined, while most residents live near the coast.
US states by total area.Florida: The state is so flat that its highest point, Britton Hill, is only 345 feet high.
US states by total area.Colorado: Its lowest point sits above 3,000 feet, so it has the highest average elevation of any state.
US states by total area.Montana: It is bigger than Germany, and its name comes from the Spanish word for mountainous.
US states by total area.California: It is the most populous state, and bigger than Japan in area.
US states by total area.Texas: It is larger than any European country except Russia and Ukraine.
US states by total area.Alaska: More than twice the size of Texas, with more coastline than all other states combined.

Birth years of great engineers and inven.Archimedes: This Greek of Syracuse explained levers and buoyancy, designed war machines for his city, and died when Romans took it in 212 BC.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Leonardo da Vinci: He sketched helicopters, tanks and flying machines centuries early, though almost none were built in his lifetime.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.James Watt: His separate condenser made steam engines far more efficient; he also coined 'horsepower', and the watt honours him.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.George Stephenson: Called the Father of Railways, he built the Rocket, and his 4 ft 8½ in track width is still standard in much of the world.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Isambard Kingdom Brunel: He built the Great Western Railway and the SS Great Britain, an iron ship driven by a screw propeller.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Gustave Eiffel: His firm built the 1889 tower that bears his name, and he also engineered the internal frame of the Statue of Liberty.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Karl Benz: His Patent-Motorwagen of 1886 is the first practical car; his wife Bertha drove it about 100 km in 1888 as the first road trip.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Henry Ford: He didn't invent the car, but his moving assembly line in 1913 cut Model T chassis assembly from over twelve hours to about ninety minutes.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Orville Wright: He was the pilot on the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk, which lasted 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet.
Birth years of great engineers and inven.Wernher von Braun: This German rocket engineer designed the V-2, then led the team behind the Saturn V that took Apollo astronauts to the Moon.

Deep time: when did these creatures live.Dickinsonia: Dickinsonia was a flat, ribbed oval creature that lived on the seafloor, and some scientists think it may be among the earliest animals.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Anomalocaris: Anomalocaris was a Cambrian predator up to about a meter long, with grasping appendages and a ring of plate-like teeth.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Dunkleosteus: Dunkleosteus was an armored fish about 6 m long whose jaw plates worked like shears, with an enormous bite force.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Meganeura (giant dragonfly): Meganeura was a dragonfly relative with a wingspan of about 70 cm, the largest known flying insect ever.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Lystrosaurus: Lystrosaurus survived the Great Dying and spread across the continents afterward, in some places making up most land vertebrates.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Ichthyosaurus: Ichthyosaurus was a dolphin-like marine reptile that gave birth to live young at sea and breathed air.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Quetzalcoatlus: Quetzalcoatlus was a giraffe-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of about 10 m. It's named after the Aztec feathered serpent god.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Titanoboa: Titanoboa was a snake about 13 m long, found in Colombian coal mines, and it lived in a warm, steamy rainforest.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Megalodon: Megalodon was a huge shark, perhaps 15 m long, and mostly known from its teeth, which can be as big as a human hand.
Deep time: when did these creatures live.Smilodon: Smilodon, the saber-toothed cat, had canines of about 18 cm. Hundreds of its skeletons were pulled out of the La Brea Tar Pits.

Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Luna 20: Luna 20 was a Soviet automatic mission that returned from the Apollonius highlands, and it collected its sample by drill.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Luna 16: Luna 16 in 1970 was the first robotic sample return from another world, bringing back soil from the Sea of Fertility.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Luna 24: Luna 24 in 1976 drilled about 2 m into the Moon and was the last lunar sample return until 2020.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Chang'e 5: China's Chang'e 5 in 2020 gathered young volcanic rock from the Oceanus Procellarum, about 2 billion years old.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Chang'e 6: Chang'e 6 in 2024 was the first mission to collect samples from the Moon's far side, from the South Pole-Aitken basin.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Apollo 11: Apollo 11 brought the first Moon rocks to Earth in 1969, and samples from it were shared with scientists around the world.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Apollo 12: Apollo 12 landed near Surveyor 3, an earlier probe, and the astronauts took parts from it home to study.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Apollo 15: Apollo 15 was the first mission with a Lunar Rover, which allowed astronauts to range farther and bring back more samples, including the Genesis Rock.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Apollo 16: Apollo 16 explored the lunar highlands and brought back rocks that helped show the Moon's crust is old.
Moon rocks brought home, by mission.Apollo 17: Apollo 17 was the last crewed Moon landing, and geologist Harrison Schmitt found orange volcanic glass on the surface.

Islands by population.Greenland: Greenland is the world's largest island, but its population is tiny, as most of it is covered by an ice sheet.
Islands by population.Iceland: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, and it runs almost entirely on geothermal and hydroelectric energy.
Islands by population.Puerto Rico: Puerto Rico is a US territory, and the Spanish and English are both official languages there.
Islands by population.Ireland: Ireland is split between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland, and it has no native snakes.
Islands by population.Cuba: Cuba is the largest Caribbean island, and it has more than 100 species of orchids.
Islands by population.Taiwan: Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced computer chips, and its capital Taipei is home to a once-tallest skyscraper.
Islands by population.Madagascar: Madagascar is home to lemurs, and most of its wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth.
Islands by population.Great Britain: Great Britain is the largest island in Europe, and it's the ninth largest island in the world.
Islands by population.Honshu: Honshu is Japan's main island, and it holds Tokyo, Kyoto and Mount Fuji.
Islands by population.Java: Java is one of the most densely populated places on Earth, and it contains Indonesia's capital, Jakarta.

Spelling and script reforms, by year.Webster's American spellings: Noah Webster's dictionary dropped the 'u' from colour and swapped -re for -er, shaping American spelling for good.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Swedish reform (hv to v): Swedish dropped the silent 'h' in words like 'hvad', which became 'vad'. The same cleaning-up spirit reached many Nordic languages.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Russian reform (drops ѣ): The Bolsheviks dropped letters like the yat (ѣ), saving print space. Plans for the reform were actually drafted before the revolution.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Japanese tōyō kanji list: It limited everyday kanji to 1,850 characters and simplified many forms to speed up postwar literacy.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Danish aa becomes å: Danish also stopped capitalising nouns that year, something German still does.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Simplified Chinese: The mainland cut strokes in thousands of characters to boost literacy. Taiwan and Hong Kong still use traditional characters.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Indonesian EYD spelling: Indonesia and Malaysia aligned their spelling, so 'tj' became 'c' and 'dj' became 'j', for instance.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Portuguese Orthographic Accord: It aimed to unify Brazilian and Portuguese spelling. It only took effect in practice from 2009 onwards.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.German spelling reform: It changed ß rules after short vowels and was so controversial it was partly revised in 2006.
Spelling and script reforms, by year.Spanish RAE Ortografía: Drawn up with Spain's and Latin America's language academies, it renamed the letter 'y' as 'ye'.

When these sitcoms aired their series fi.The Mary Tyler Moore Show: Ended with the newsroom crew's tearful group hug, and then everyone reached for the tissues.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.M*A*S*H: 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen' drew about 105 million US viewers, a record that stood for decades.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.Cheers: The finale drew about 80 million viewers, and Sam ends up alone at the bar he loves.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.Seinfeld: The last episode sent the four main characters to jail for violating a Good Samaritan law.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.Friends: About 52 million Americans watched Rachel get off the plane.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.Everybody Loves Raymond: It ran for nine seasons, and star Ray Romano drew on his own family life.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.Scrubs: Based loosely on the experiences of Dr Jonathan Doris, a friend of creator Bill Lawrence.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.The Office (US): Adapted from Ricky Gervais's British series, it closed with Dwight's wedding.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.How I Met Your Mother: The ending was so contentious in part because the kids' scenes were filmed in 2006.
When these sitcoms aired their series fi.The Big Bang Theory: Ran 12 seasons, making it the longest-running multi-camera sitcom in US history.

Elements named after scientists, by atom.Curium: Named for Marie and Pierre Curie; curium-244 powers the alpha-particle X-ray spectrometers on several Mars rovers.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Einsteinium: First found in the debris of the 1952 Ivy Mike hydrogen bomb test, and kept secret for a few years afterward.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Fermium: Also discovered in H-bomb fallout; named for Enrico Fermi, who built the world's first nuclear reactor in Chicago.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Mendelevium: Named for Dmitri Mendeleev, who drew up the periodic table; the first experiment made only a handful of atoms.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Nobelium: Named for Alfred Nobel, and its discovery was disputed for years among labs in Sweden, the US and the Soviet Union.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Rutherfordium: Named for Ernest Rutherford, who showed atoms have a tiny dense nucleus; it exists only briefly, made in labs.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Seaborgium: Glenn Seaborg was still alive when this was named in his honor in 1997, a rare distinction; he co-discovered ten elements.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Bohrium: Named for Niels Bohr, whose model put electrons in set orbits around the nucleus; it lasts only seconds.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Copernicium: Named for Nicolaus Copernicus, who placed the Sun at the center of the solar system; the name was announced on his birthday.
Elements named after scientists, by atom.Oganesson: The heaviest element known, named for Yuri Oganessian, who was only the second person honored while still living.

When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Welch's grape juice: Thomas Welch, a dentist, pasteurized grape juice so churches could serve non-alcoholic communion wine.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Ovaltine: Invented in Switzerland as Ovomaltine, and the name was misspelled when registered in Britain.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Kool-Aid: Edwin Perkins of Hastings, Nebraska, made it as a powder to cut the shipping cost of liquid drinks.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Hawaiian Punch: It started as a syrup topping for ice cream, before it was sold as a drink.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Tropicana: Anthony Rossi began it in Florida, and it helped make orange juice a breakfast staple.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Tang: William Mitchell developed it for General Foods, and John Glenn drank it in 1962.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.SunnyD: Introduced in Florida as 'Sunny Delight', it is known as a tangy orange drink.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Capri-Sun: A German pouch drink with a foil pack and a straw; it was brought to the US in the 1980s.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Snapple: It started in Brooklyn as a health-food juice store.
When these drink brands for kids (and ki.Vitaminwater: Coca-Cola bought its maker, Glacéau, for 4.1 billion dollars in 2007.

Instruments and bells by weight.Violin: A fine Stradivarius violin can be worth millions. They were made in Cremona, Italy, around the turn of the 18th century, and no one has quite matched them.
Instruments and bells by weight.Trumpet: Early trumpets lacked valves and could play only a handful of notes. Today's three-valve version dates to the early 19th century.
Instruments and bells by weight.Acoustic guitar: Guitars descend from older instruments like the lute, and the six-string form took shape in Spain. Their hollow body amplifies the strings' vibrations.
Instruments and bells by weight.Tuba: The tuba is the biggest brass instrument, and its coiled tube, if unwound, would stretch around five metres or more. It was invented in 1835 in Prussia.
Instruments and bells by weight.Concert harp: It has 47 strings and seven pedals that change the pitch of each note. Its strings are tensioned to a total pull of roughly a tonne or more.
Instruments and bells by weight.Upright piano: Upright pianos were designed to fit into smaller homes by turning the strings vertical. Many can reach well over 200 kg.
Instruments and bells by weight.Concert grand piano: A concert grand has about 230 strings pulled with a combined tension of around 20 tonnes. Its iron frame is what holds it all together.
Instruments and bells by weight.Liberty Bell: This Philadelphia icon cracked soon after arriving in 1752 and was recast twice. It became a symbol of freedom, especially for abolitionists.
Instruments and bells by weight.Big Ben (the bell): Big Ben is the bell, not the tower, which is named Elizabeth Tower. It has chimed from Westminster since 1859, and also developed a crack soon after.
Instruments and bells by weight.Tsar Bell: This giant Moscow bell has never rung. It cracked in a fire in 1737 before it was lifted from its casting pit, and now sits on display in the Kremlin.

Bug-eaters by weight.Pipistrelle bat: A single pipistrelle can eat many thousands of midges in one night. Though tiny, it can live for up to about 16 years.
Bug-eaters by weight.Swallow: Swallows catch insects in flight and even drink and wash on the wing. Each autumn they migrate from Europe to southern Africa, thousands of kilometres.
Bug-eaters by weight.Great spotted woodpecker: It hammers on trees to find grubs, and a special bone structure around its skull cushions the impact. Its tongue wraps around the back of its head.
Bug-eaters by weight.Veiled chameleon: Chameleons shoot out their sticky tongues faster than the eye can follow to snatch insects. Their eyes can move independently, looking two ways at once.
Bug-eaters by weight.Hedgehog: A hedgehog can eat beetles, worms, slugs and caterpillars, making it a gardener's friend. Lawn chemicals and lost hedgerows have caused its decline.
Bug-eaters by weight.Echidna: This spiny, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has a long, sticky tongue for ants and termites. It has no teeth and crushes food against its palate.
Bug-eaters by weight.Pangolin: Covered in scales made of keratin, like your fingernails, pangolins curl into a ball when threatened. They are heavily trafficked, which has made them critically endangered.
Bug-eaters by weight.Giant anteater: It can flick its tongue out about 150 times a minute and eat tens of thousands of ants and termites a day. It has no teeth at all.
Bug-eaters by weight.Aardvark: A single aardvark can scoop up tens of thousands of termites in a night using its long, sticky tongue. Its burrows also shelter many other animals.
Bug-eaters by weight.Sloth bear: This shaggy South Asian bear sucks up termites through a gap in its teeth, with a lip that closes its nostrils. Mothers carry cubs on their backs.

India through history.Indus Valley cities flourish: Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa had grid streets and drains, and their script remains undeciphered.
India through history.Maurya Empire founded: Chandragupta founded it, and later Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the brutal Kalinga war.
India through history.Gupta Empire founded: Often called India's Golden Age, with advances in mathematics including zero as a numeral.
India through history.Delhi Sultanate begins: Ruled by dynasties including Qutb ud-din Aibak, who began the Qutb Minar.
India through history.Mughal Empire founded: Babur won at Panipat, and the dynasty ruled for over three centuries.
India through history.British East India Company: Chartered by Elizabeth I, this trading firm eventually ruled much of India.
India through history.Taj Mahal completed: Shah Jahan built it for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and the work took around 20 years.
India through history.Rebellion of 1857: It began as a soldiers' mutiny in Meerut, and afterwards the British Crown took over rule from the company.
India through history.Independence: India gained independence on 15 August, along with the Partition into India and Pakistan.
India through history.Republic Day: India's constitution came into force on 26 January, marked by an annual parade in New Delhi.
